title: Beyond the Active Site: Allosteric Tail of HIV-1 Protease Is a Potential Target for Inhibiting Dimerization.
one_liner_zh: 该文通过高级分子动力学模拟研究HIV-1蛋白酶单体与抑制剂的别构结合，揭示尾部口袋抑制二聚化的机制，属于蛋白质构象采样与结构计算问题，方法为物理模拟，与课题高度相关。
abstract: HIV protease (HIVPR) is one of the key targets in AIDS therapy. All ten FDA-approved drugs targeting this enzyme compete with the substrates in binding to its active site. However, the emergence of drug-resistant mutants in active and nonactive sites of HIVPR has compromised the efficacy of these drugs. Nonetheless, darunavir (DRV) and tipranavir (TPV) have exhibited greater success than the other eight drugs, presumably due to their dual mode of action: (i) inhibiting protease activity and (ii) blocking protease dimerization. Although crystal structures have explained the inhibitory mechanism of protease activity, the mechanism of inhibiting the dimerization process is poorly understood. In this study, we employ advanced molecular dynamics simulation methods to identify the precise binding motifs of DRV and TPV with monomeric HIVPR. Our results suggest that both inhibitors bind stably to an allosteric pocket located in the tail region of the enzyme. Results also elucidate reversible association-dissociation of the drugs between the conventional active site and the newly identified tail cavity through surface diffusion. Structural analysis revealed that drug binding to the tail pocket induces a conformational extension of the C-terminal alpha-helix, a change that sequesters the terminal residues required for stable dimer formation. Our finding aligns very well with the reported ESI-MS spectra showing the tail interface as a crucial domain in forming a stable HIV protease dimer. Our result paves the way for designing a new class of HIVPR drugs that could target the C-terminal to effectively lock it in the monomeric form, potentially bypassing the cross-resistance due to active-site mutations.
abstract_zh: HIV蛋白酶（HIVPR）是艾滋病治疗中的关键靶点之一。所有十种FDA批准的针对该酶的药物均与底物竞争结合其活性位点。然而，HIVPR活性位点及非活性位点耐药突变体的出现已削弱了这些药物的疗效。尽管如此，达芦那韦（DRV）和替拉那韦（TPV）相比其他八种药物表现出更大的成功，推测归因于其双重作用模式：（i）抑制蛋白酶活性及（ii）阻断蛋白酶二聚化。尽管晶体结构已解释了蛋白酶活性的抑制机制，但抑制二聚化过程的机制仍知之甚少。在本研究中，我们采用先进的分子动力学模拟方法，以识别DRV和TPV与单体HIVPR的精确结合基序。我们的结果表明，两种抑制剂均稳定结合于酶尾部区域的一个别构口袋。结果还阐明了药物在常规活性位点与新识别的尾部腔之间通过表面扩散进行的可逆结合-解离过程。结构分析揭示，药物结合尾部口袋诱导C端α-螺旋的构象延伸，这一变化隔离了稳定二聚体形成所需的末端残基。我们的发现与已报道的ESI-MS谱图高度一致，表明尾部界面是形成稳定HIV蛋白酶二聚体的关键结构域。我们的结果为设计新型HIVPR药物铺平了道路，这些药物可靶向C端以有效将其锁定在单体形式，从而可能绕过因活性位点突变导致的交叉耐药性。
